newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Baywatch star sells wrinkle cream in Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: Baywatch star sells wrinkle cream in Hong Kong.

text.p: David Hasselhoff, creator and star of the hit television show "Baywatch", has a new job hawking wrinkle cream for people that want to look as good as he does.
"While I like to think of myself as a good actor, on Baywatch looking good is about 90 percent of it and learning how to run down the beach in slow motion is very important," Hasselhoff said.
Looking tall, tanned and younger than his 44 years, the actor and singer was in Hong Kong making a pitch for Ethocyn, a new skin-care product by Los Angeles-based Chantal Pharmaceutical Corp.

Chantal is hoping that the astounding popularity of Baywatch -- a programme that is short on plot but long on sand, sun and scantily clad specimens of both sexes -- will be a boon to its cosmetics line.
The show has one billion viewers worldwide, more than 200 million of which are in Asia.
While Ethocyn will not be formally launched in Asia until next March, the promoters were in town because Hasselhoff is on his way to Taipei for a weekend gig singing at the Hard Rock Cafe.

Hasselhoff's publicist declined to reveal how much her client makes to speak for Ethocyn, his first product endorsement, but the star quipped that "it is less than what Michael Jordan gets from Nike".
Hasselhoff said he first came across Ethocyn on the Baywatch set because his female co-stars were using it to ward off the effects of hours spent in the sun.

Most of the stars of Baywatch are much younger than the 35- to 60-year-old women and men that Ethocyn is targeting and none show any signs of sagging skin, although Hasselhoff fits into that age group.
Hasselhoff made headlines in Hong Kong when it was revealed that home-town hero Lee Lai-shan politely declined his invitation to a dinner party because she had to study for an exam.

Hasselhoff, seemingly unaware of the news blitz that has surrounded windsurfer Lee since she brought home Hong Kong's first-ever Olympic gold medal, said he thought the front-page South China Morning Post story was the strangest he had ever seen. But he met with Lee briefly.
"We invited her to come on the show when she's in L.A.," he said.
